propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui beatum Cyrillum Confessorem tuum atque Pontificem divinae
maternitatis beatissimae Virginis Mariae assertorem invictum effecisti:
concede, ipso intercedente; ut, qui vere eam Genetricem Dei credimus,
materna ejusdem protectione salvemur. Per eundem Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n912, printed p. 914, running head `FEB. 9-ST. CYRIL OF ALEXANDRIA, B. C.`, under `Prayer` in the Mass headed `St. Cyril of Alexandria, Bishop, Confessor, Doctor of the Church`. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer; the witness spells `Genitricem` where 1962 spells `Genetricem` and prints the conclusion cue `Per eumdem Dominum` where 1962 expands the conclusion. The book itself prints Cyril's name, title and English, so no name or wording is supplied by this inventory.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O God, Who didst make blessed Cyril, Thy Confessor and Bishop, the invincible champion of the most blessed Virgin Mary's divine maternity, grant through his intercession that we, who verily believe her to be the Mother of God, may be saved by her maternal protection. Through the same.

ordinary_disposition.basis: Printed after the Postcommunions as an alternative Epistle for Doctors.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Munera nostra, omnipotens Deus, benignus respice: et, intercedente beato
Cyrillo, praesta; ut unigenitum tuum Jesum Christum Dominum nostrum, in
tua tecum gloria coaeternum, in cordibus nostris digne suscipere
mereamur: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n912, printed p. 914, under `Secret`, and finishes on leaf n913, printed p. 915; both leaves were opened. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer, with differences only in pointing and the witness's abbreviation of the conclusion to `Qui tecum`.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: Look with kindness, O almighty God, upon our gifts and, through the intercession of blessed Cyril, grant that we may worthily take into our hearts Thine only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, Who with Thee.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Divinis, Domine, refecti mysteriis, te supplices deprecamur: ut, exemplis
et meritis beati Cyrilli Pontificis adjuti, sanctissimae Genetrici
Unigeniti tui digne famulari valeamus: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in
unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n913, printed p. 915, under `Postcommunion` in the Mass of St Cyril. The Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer; the witness spells `Genitrici` where 1962 spells `Genetrici` and abbreviates the conclusion to `Qui tecum`.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: Refreshed with the divine mysteries, O Lord, we humbly beseech Thee that, aided by the examples and the merits of blessed Cyril Thy Bishop, we may be able to serve worthily the most holy Mother of Thine only-begotten Son, Who with Thee liveth.
